sub: Climate Risk Mapping for Snacks Portfolio
ctx: Environmental Defense Fund Climate Corps. First-choice placement, selected from 1,000+ applicants.
challenge: As a 2025 EDF Climate Corps Fellow, I worked with PepsiCo’s Global Sustainability Office to address increasing climate risks in India. Rising temperatures, water stress, and shifting consumer expectations are creating challenges for food security and operations. The project evaluated vulnerabilities in key product categories and identified resilience strategies to strengthen PepsiCo’s ability to deliver against growth ambitions in climate-sensitive markets.
solution: I approached the challenge through research, stakeholder interviews, and cross-functional analysis, engaging leaders across risk management, R&D, agriculture, finance, and packaging. The work centered on three areas: oil sourcing and stability, packaging resilience, and shelf-life implications for core snack categories. I reviewed regional data, gathered perspectives on consumer preferences and packaging innovation, and developed a framework linking climate-related challenges with product strategy and innovation pathways.
impact: The work brought together perspectives on oil stability, packaging performance, and consumer trends, surfacing insights across functions and regions that might otherwise have stayed siloed. It offered findings to guide future conversations and investment, connecting climate risk awareness with product and market decisions.
note: Adapted from my EDF Climate Corps project page.
title: PepsiCo, Global Sustainability Office: Climate Risk Mapping for Snacks Portfolio
